source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Maldesecco is a fungal dieback disease of citrus, caused by a fungus known locally by its Italian name (meaning "bad dry"). It enters through wounds and damaged tissue and progressively kills back twigs and branches from the tip inward; infected shoots show a characteristic yellowing/bronzing (chlorosis) before dying, and cutting into affected wood often reveals a pinkish or salmon-colored discoloration inside the stem.

Symptoms typically begin on young shoots and progress toward older wood if untreated, and trees that are already stressed (from drought, waterlogging, or physical damage) are more susceptible to infection and to severe dieback once infected.

Management includes pruning out and destroying infected twigs and branches well below the visible symptom line, disinfecting pruning tools between cuts to avoid spreading the fungus, avoiding wounding trees unnecessarily, and applying a copper-based fungicide such as a Bordeaux mixture to cut surfaces and to the tree as a protective spray during humid periods when infection risk is highest.
